newsitem.title: USA: Memories have some afraid to short muni contract.
newsitem.headline: Memories have some afraid to short muni contract.

text.p: The spectre of alleged manipulation that haunted some recent municipal futures contract settlements has players fearful of shorting the December contract ahead of Thursday's expiration.

The contract, which is cash settled at the price of the Bond Buyer's 40-bond index, traded at as much as a 10/32 premium to the index during Wednesday's session, a trader said. The December contract however closed at 116-15/32, just a 2/32 premium over the 40-bond index at 116-13/32.

"The reason that they are in close alignment is because they smashed the (contracts) in the last 10 minutes," the trader said. "Ten minutes before had it gone out it would have been closing at an eight to 10 tick premium."
The trader said he had "no idea" why the municipal and government contracts got hit near the close. "They just started hitting it for no good reason, it got hit pretty good at the close," he said.

The fact that the muni contract was trading at such a premium so close to the close is indicative of the "long memories" players have, the trader said. They are afraid to be caught short should index bonds experience a sharp run up, he said.
Some players expressed concerns to the Chicago Board of trade in June, citing the heightened performance of the 40-bond index versus the overall market, which it is supposed to mirror.
While some players found the disparity troubling, others said if index bonds were outperforming the broader market, those holding index bonds should have taken advantage of it.
On Wednesday quite a few index bonds were out for the bid, so it would taken a large amount of buying to drive the index higher, the trader said.
